label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Hi Mikaela, yep we started on 21 Sept, after mating had started. Happy to give you the warts and all version, especially after how much you helped us when Dave did his shoulder.

We’re milking 290, mostly 3-way crossbreds. We’ve dropped Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday arvo milkings, so four once-a-days a week. Mornings are still 5.15 every day. Not quite a sleep-in arrangement unfortunately!

Going off the Fonterra app, milksolids are down about 6% on the same weeks last year. The rep had told us to expect 8–10%, so it’s been better than we’d braced for. That’s only comparing this season with last though, not saying all of that is down to the milking change. And we haven’t been through a whole season of it yet, so ask me again in March.

Cells did jump. We were about 110,000 before and got up around 180,000 in the first three weeks. Back around 135,000 now. So they didn’t go completely mental, but I wouldn’t tell you there was no effect either.

The worst bit was a heifer with mastitis that went bad on a skipped arvo. Didn’t pick her up till the next morning and we lost a quarter. That’s the bit I’d really want you to know before deciding. You still have to check cows on the skip days, and you’ve got to be right on top of teat spraying. An afternoon without milking can’t mean nobody looking at the cows. It’ll bite you if you let things slide.

The cows settled into it quicker than I expected. About four days of bellowing at the gate, then they seemed quite happy with the new arrangement.

Lameness has been a big improvement here. Four on the lame list now against eleven this time last year. Our back paddocks are a 1.8km walk, so fewer trips must be helping. Again, that’s our place and our comparison with last year, but it’s a difference we’re very pleased to see.

For us the biggest thing has been what it’s done for the people. Kieran said it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. That probably tells you more than I can about the hours.

The first Sunday arvo we skipped, Dave and I went over to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday off in spring in twenty-odd years. Felt very odd not having to get back for milking, but we got over that fairly quickly!

Honestly, I wouldn’t go back. The hours alone are worth the 6% to us. But that’s us weighing it up, not me promising you’ll get the same result. I’d hate you to go into it thinking there’s no production cost or extra watching needed. If Tom’s knees are that bad though, I reckon those arvos off would help him more than anything, and I can understand wanting to make things better for your young fella too.

Come and grab me at the field day on the 19th. I’ll bring our shed rosters and numbers along and you can have a proper look at what we’re doing, bad bits included.

Or ring me whenever you want. Much easier than texting with these useless thumbs.
